text:
maria: heads-up — after landing the coalesce-delay bump to 2.5ms we saw a 12-18% p95 latency drift on the small-req tail in prod. noticed at ~08:30 UTC, correlates with kernel-switch traffic peaks.

aj: oof. did you capture a flame or perf trace?
	maria: grabbed a quick perf record and a couple traces. attaching stack snippet: ```
# perf script excerpt
[kernel] microbatch_coalesce+0x1a2
[userspace] runtime::dispatch_batch
[userspace] kernel_selector::choose
```

	tomas: any change in kv cache hit rates during that window? if prefix cache drops, we could be re-warming big KV pages and triggering slower kernels.
	maria: yes — KV-prefix hit dropped ~7% for token budgets >512 in the ~5m window. sequence: coalesce delay up, jitter widened, more heterogeneous batch sizes, cache churn up.
	katie: quick hypothesis: increased jitter caused micro-windows to align less, increasing partial batches that push different seq-lens together — runtime picks generic kernel instead of fast-fused kernel for long-short mixes.
	aj: got a profiling tarball, ran the kernel-selection heatmap. short summary: when batch contains >25% short seqs (<64) and >10% long seqs (>512) we pick fallback matmul kernel that has worse throughput for long outputs.
	maria: timeline: 08:29 deploy -> coalesce_delay=2.5ms, jitter=0.8ms; 08:31 p95 drift starts; 08:35 KV hit drop; 08:40 autoscale added one node, latency transiently improved.
	ci-bot: deploy recorded: coalesce_delay=2.5ms, jitter=0.8ms, microbatch_interval=0.75ms, commit sha abc123
	tomas: can you paste the small experiment results we ran on staging? I remember we had a variant with jitter_floor=0.15ms that avoided the mixed-size batches.
	maria: staging replay:
```
config A: coalesce=2.5ms jitter=0.8ms -> p95 +15%
config B: coalesce=2.5ms jitter=0.15ms -> p95 +3%
config C: coalesce=1.5ms jitter=0.15ms -> p95 -2%
```
	katie: so two levers: reduce coalesce delay or tighten jitter. reducing coalesce buys less aggregation but keeps batch shape consistent; tightening jitter avoids pathological interleaving.
	aj: also consider token_budget_target enforcement per queue. we saw queues with high token caps occasionally pulling in long requests into mostly-short batches. if we cap token_budget for short-optimized lanes to 256, kernel_selector stays biased to fused kernels.
	maria: action plan proposal: 1) rollback jitter to 0.15ms on prod canary, 2) add a soft token_budget ceiling for short-priority queue = 256, 3) enable a temporary kernel-selection metric (emit chosen_kernel label) for 30m to validate.
	tomas: agree. also add KV-prefetch priming for lanes that miss >5% KVs in 1m window to reduce re-warm thrash.
	katie: quick synthetic to validate: run 20m mixed replay with current traffic mix and new config B + token cap; measure p50/p95 + kernel distribution. I can run at 09:10.
	aj: i'm going to instrument the selector to log histograms by batch-composition. will roll a debug build to canary and tag traces.
	maria: rolling canary now to 10% with jitter=0.15ms & short_token_cap=256. will watch KV hit and kernel labels.
	ci-bot: canary started at 09:02 UTC, target shards: 3, rollout=10%
	maria: initial metrics: KV hit recovers to baseline after ~90s, chosen_kernel=fused_matmul spikes to 42% (was 18%), p95 trending down after 2m.
	katie: nice. leave canary for 30m, then widen if stable. also annotate the run in perf-dashboard with the kernel labels.
	aj: note for follow-up: we should add a batching heuristic that penalizes mixing >2 size classes in same microbatch and instead wait up to an extra 0.5ms to align similar seq-lens. could be a smarter coalesce policy.
	maria: filing a short RFC for that heuristic — will include metrics to justify the extra wait time tradeoff.
	tomas: fft. thanks everyone. please post short findings in the microbatch tuning doc and link the canary dashboard. :thumbsup:
	maria: will do. linking dashboard: https://perf.internal.redwood/dashboards/microbatch/1712345678-canary
	aj: and the perf tarball: s3://redwood-perf/microbatch/1712345678.tar.gz
	maria: closing loop — after 30m canary we widened to 50% with same configs, p95 remained within +1% of baseline. pushing full rollback to jitter=0.15ms and token cap applied.
	katie: great outcome. next items: RFC for composition-aware coalesce + automated kernel-selection telemetry.
	maria: thanks all.
